candidates.tagline: They built a biometric border system for 500M arrivals — with no pre-registration.
candidates.story: The EU's Entry/Exit System launched April 10, 2026 requiring all non-EU travellers to submit fingerprints and a face scan at the physical border with zero advance pre-registration option, generating five-hour queues at summer peak checkpoints; on July 1, airlines wrote to the EU Commission demanding emergency suspension, and Rome airport CEO Marco Troncone told the Financial Times the chaos is 'not a matter of implementation — it's a design flaw.'
candidates.why_funny: Bureaucrats spent years and billions deploying a 'smart' biometric border upgrade that forces every single traveller to do their full enrollment in person, at the bottleneck, at peak summer travel — exactly when standing in a five-hour queue is least tolerable.
candidates.alt: Travellers packed into a long, congested queue at Brussels Zaventem airport at a border control checkpoint, illustrating the delays caused by the EU Entry/Exit System biometric rollout in summer 2026

candidates.tagline: Boeing spent $4.8 billion on a space taxi NASA now doubts will ever carry passengers.
candidates.story: A NASA Inspector General report published July 1, 2026 formally expressed doubt that Boeing's CST-100 Starliner will ever achieve human-rating certification — after $4.8 billion spent, repeated helium leaks, propulsion failures, and unresolved parachute anomalies — explicitly citing 'overconfidence in Boeing's heritage systems' and 'unrealistic launch schedules' as root causes, with the ISS due to retire around 2030.
candidates.why_funny: Boeing convinced NASA and Congress to fund a multi-decade space taxi entirely on the premise that their old aerospace skills were still reliable — the Inspector General's report is the official confirmation that they were not.
candidates.alt: Boeing's CST-100 Starliner spacecraft undocking from the International Space Station following its Crew Flight Test mission in 2024, floating in orbit with the Earth's limb visible below
